PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use windowed delivery for state channels
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Adds one shared channel layer for Agent Host Protocol windowed delivery. TCP streams and state
channels (sessions, chats, terminals, changesets, automations) now use this layer on the agent host
and on the client. Large snapshots go as `channel/frame` fragments with flow control. Thus they do
not exceed transport frame limits and do not block other channels on the connection.

- Adds `AgentHostChannelSubscription`. It owns the window, queues, reassembly, snapshots, and
  failure behavior for one peer's subscription. A per-channel policy sets the buffer bounds,
  the reset method, adjacent action coalescing, and snapshot validation.
- Moves TCP streams onto the shared subscription. The public TCP API does not change.
- The client offers windowed delivery for all state channels except root. The host accepts on
  transports that keep the original message sizes. Peers that do not offer or accept windowing
  keep ordinary delivery.
- Adds one per-connection channel registry on the host. It sends each `subscribe` and `reconnect`
  response before the channel starts. It also routes incoming and outgoing channel messages for TCP
  and state channels through one path.
- Windowed subscriptions recover by snapshot after reconnect. The client does not apply a
  `subscribe` result that arrives after it unsubscribed. It holds channel data while a windowed
  `subscribe` is in progress.
- State channels use a 1 MiB window and frames of up to 16 MiB. The backlog limit does not count
  the message that is in progress, so one large snapshot is never refused.
- The receiver batches credit. It sends credit when three quarters of the window is uncredited,
  or at most 5 seconds after the first uncredited release. TCP sends credit at once on EOF.
- Logs each delivery failure that drops a connection or channel as a warning, and reports it as
  `agentHost.channelFailure` telemetry with a bounded reason code.
- A failure in a notification handler on a state channel no longer closes the connection.
- The scheduler no longer reserves a full frame before each send. This stops one small message per
  timer turn on channels with large frames.
- The local automation store no longer subscribes again to the same connection at startup.

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window against a local or remote agent host built from this branch.
2. Open a large chat and a terminal, then disconnect and reconnect the host.
3. In the AHP JSONL logs, state subscriptions offer `flowControl`, large snapshots arrive as
   `channel/frame` fragments, and reconnect keeps windowed channels with `snapshot` recovery.
4. `renderer.log` and `agenthost.log` contain no `[AgentHostChannels] ... failed` warnings.

To make nearly every state message fragment locally, temporarily set
`agentHostStateReceiveLimits.maximumFrameBytes` in `common/agentHostChannel.ts` to `1024`.

## Validation

With Node 24.22.1 and dependencies from `pnpm i`, after merging `origin/main`:

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed, no errors.
- `pnpm run eslint <changed agent host files>`: passed, 277 files, no warnings.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"`: 17018 passed,
  1 failed. The failure is `Mission Control projects > GitHub SSH and scp URLs clone over HTTPS
  with the authenticated bearer`. This test also fails on the base commit without this change.
- `./scripts/test.sh` for `agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts` and
  `editorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient.test.ts`: 144 passed.
- Manual Code OSS runs with 1 KiB frames: no dropped connections from windowed delivery.
  Three soft reconnects to a remote host kept every windowed channel and recovered each one from
  its snapshot. A host restart recovered through a fresh initialize.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/339997
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335232

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added state snapshot call, default 256 KiB effective fragment cap, repeated prefix character access after concatenation, and client await path are all traced. V8's flattening of non-flat cons strings establishes the copying mechanism; exact snapshot prevalence and wall-clock cost are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer string-prefix copying, transient UTF-16 buffers, and garbage collection
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a snapshot of S UTF-16-accounted bytes fragmented into F frames, prefix flattening copies O(S*F) bytes, approximately O(S^2/B) for effective payload size B at most 256 KiB. For example, 25 MiB of accounted snapshot text requires at least 100 fragments before escaping overhead and repeatedly copies roughly a gigabyte of prefixes. Concurrent restored channels add their individual costs.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Superlinear renderer CPU/allocation cost, GC pressure, and increased chat-open/reconnect latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: State subscribe returned the snapshot in one JSON-RPC response, serialized and parsed as a whole with linear string processing. The prefix-flattening reassembler was only reached by the existing bounded TCP delivery path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every accepted non-root state subscription now sends its full snapshot through the channel reassembler, with frames capped at 256 KiB and no client snapshot-size bound, newly applying repeated prefix flattening to large conversation histories.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added sendSnapshot(snapshot) at agentHostConnectionChannels.ts:57 routes state snapshots through fragmented AgentHostChannelDelivery for the first time. protocolServerHandler.ts:2235 now returns only flowControl instead of the ordinary snapshot response, and agentHostProtocolClient.ts:2114 waits for the separately reassembled snapshot. Previously only bounded TCP messages used this reassembler; state snapshot delivery did not perform repeated prefix character accesses.
Findings.Title: Avoid flattening every prefix when reassembling large snapshots
Findings.Impact: Opening or reconnecting a chat with multi-megabyte conversation/tool-output history now repeatedly copies its accumulated snapshot on the renderer, causing CPU/GC pressure and delaying snapshot readiness; larger histories produce increasingly long main-thread work.
Findings.Evidence: StateChannel.start now calls AgentHostChannelSubscription.sendSnapshot, whose delivery sendFrame fragments at at most 256 KiB (agentHostChannelDelivery.ts:349,409-435), despite the 16 MiB negotiated maximum. On the renderer, accept appends each fragment to _fragments (line 510), then the next fragment reads _fragments.charCodeAt(_fragments.length - 1) (line 505). In V8, reading a non-flat concatenated string here flattens the accumulated prefix; this repeats for every fragment. The state policy permits arbitrarily large received snapshots. _requestSnapshot waits for reassembly before exposing the state, and reconnect also waits for these snapshots.
Findings.Recommendation: Accumulate fragments in an array, retain the previous fragment's final code unit separately for surrogate validation, and join once for the final JSON.parse. Preserve byte accounting and credit behavior.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Rebinding the same connected Automation facade unconditionally cleared and rebuilt its connection-scoped projection. AgentHostAutomationStore constructor reparsed the saved run archive and reacquired the entire catalogue. When the store held the last catalogue reference, disposal evicted that refcounted subscription and reacquisition issued another subscribe/snapshot request.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Redundant catalogue subscription/snapshot transfer and archive reconstruction when a connected local provider rebinds the same service at host startup; cost scales with catalogue and saved archive size rather than the number of actual connection changes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new connection identity guard returns before clearConnection for the already-bound connection. Explicit clearConnection resets the identity so genuinely new bindings still construct a fresh store.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 71 carried the unconditional clearConnection and blame identifies its introducing commit. localAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:269-285 calls bindConnection initially and again from onAgentHostStart with the same _agentHostService. AgentHostAutomationStore.ts:122-132 parses the archive and calls getSubscription during reconstruction. AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription reuses only live entries and _disposeSubscriptionEntry unsubscribes a released entry. The added CountingConnection test demonstrates two same-connection setConnection calls now acquire once, while clear/rebind acquires again.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a non-root session/chat/changeset/automation state subscription, including a large chat history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The refcounted subscription awaits subscribe, any necessary host restoration, and now the separate channel/snapshot's final fragment and JSON.parse before installing verified state. Warm state avoids restoration but not snapshot transfer/reassembly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send subscribe response followed by the full snapshot as direct channel data or JSON fragments over WebSocket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request/response per newly acquired resource and at least ceil(S/256 KiB) data frames for a large snapshot, with escaping/envelopes increasing the count; cumulative credits batch at 75% of the 1 MiB receive window or five seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One subscribe response contained the whole snapshot; no state-channel fragmentation or credit controls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Complete reassembly is required for subscription readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the same JSON protocol frames through local MessagePort or IPC bridging rather than a direct remote WebSocket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport delivery per data fragment and batched credit notification. IPC outgoing notifications use one IChannel.call('send', text) per emitted frame, not per item in the snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing local transports carried one ordinary subscribe snapshot response; transport implementations themselves are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local snapshot readiness also waits for all fragments; calls are asynchronous and the sender is window-limited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize snapshot JSON and fragment envelopes, parse each received envelope, concatenate fragment text, read the accumulated final code unit, and finally parse the full notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial snapshot serialization, per-frame serialization/parsing, and one growing-prefix character access per additional fragment. V8 prefix flattening adds O(S*F) copying rather than only linear processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Whole state snapshot serialization and parsing were linear; repeated prefix flattening only occurred on the pre-existing bounded TCP reassembler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the receiving renderer and delays final snapshot delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session registration/catalog/persisted metadata and register restored state on a cold owner restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-owner restoration sequence, joined by the _restoreSessionInFlight map; resident state bypasses the full restore. Branch-dependent database reads are not newly multiplied by window negotiation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscribe restoration and database operations preceded the ordinary snapshot response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restoration precedes snapshot generation; the newly added getSnapshot reads resident maps and does not repeat restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing provider conversation restoration, including provider SDK session resume and MCP runtime startup where applicable; persisted terminal/chat restoration may also read backing storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per cold owning-session/chat restoration, coalesced by existing owner restore state; provider-specific subprocess/filesystem details are unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider conversation restoration was awaited for ordinary subscribe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold history retrieval must finish before the snapshot is generated; warm resident snapshots do not start another runtime.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct active resource URIs after AgentSubscriptionManager refcount reuse; cold owning sessions after restoreSession in-flight coalescing; S UTF-16-accounted snapshot bytes per subscribed channel, with payload fragments bounded by an effective 256 KiB frame cap, not the negotiated 16 MiB maximum.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Different subscriptions may restore concurrently, while the same owner restore is coalesced and passive metadata work is sequenced per session. A transport-local scheduler round-robins channels, yields after 256 KiB bursts, polls buffered transports at 25 ms, and gives each channel its own window; renderer acceptance is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Refcounted manager entries reuse subscriptions by resource URI. Host getSnapshot returns resident terminal/state objects without storage access. Cold session restores join by owner/session key and successful resident state avoids repeated restoration. Failed resources may be reacquired through existing manager behavior; no new negative cache was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced from new StateChannel.sendSnapshot through effective frame sizing, renderer accept, and snapshot await. The prefix-flattening mechanism is independent of provider or transport choice.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact chat snapshot size distribution, V8 wall-clock duration, and concurrent-channel prevalence are unmeasured. Terminal retained content is capped at 100,000 characters, so the strongest trigger is large chat/tool-output histories rather than arbitrary terminal scrollback.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the new superlinear snapshot reassembly cost. Fragmentation/flow control itself is an intentional transport-safety improvement; unchanged cold restoration costs were not reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recover active windowed state channels after a soft disconnect or host restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconnect response and authentication restoration are followed by installing kept channels' complete snapshots before Connected and queued optimistic-action delivery. Client restore groups install sessions first, then chats and other channels concurrently. Fresh initialize retains ordinary initial snapshot behavior and existing restore fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send reconnect result, then one full snapshot data message per accepted kept state window, each potentially fragmented.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reconnect request/response plus one full snapshot per negotiated unique channel and batched credits. Channels omitted from window acceptance follow ordinary restore/resubscribe handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay-capable reconnect returned relevant missed actions without separately sending kept state-window snapshots; snapshot fallback included ordinary snapshots in the response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All required kept snapshots must arrive before reconnect completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reassemble each full channel snapshot and install it into the subscription manager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per-channel O(S*F) prefix copying on large snapshots; channel costs add. Client session-first installation does not serialize the host's channel transfers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relevant replay actions or whole ordinary snapshots were processed without state-channel prefix reassembly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Renderer copying and final parsing block snapshot readiness and reconnect progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore missing host state and retrieve backing conversation data when the host no longer has resident state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same existing unique-channel subscribe flow, with shared owner restores coalesced. Warm surviving host state uses resident reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconnect already subscribed/restored each distinct requested state channel, including on replay paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the reconnect response's channels start snapshot transfer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique subscribed channels after restoredUris deduplication; sum of their full snapshot sizes. Cold owner restores are coalesced by session key. Each large channel produces its own F fragments.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host uses Promise.all over requested subscriptions with URI deduplication and per-owner restore joining. Host starts channels after sending the response and uses one fair scheduler per transport. Client awaits session installation before parallel chat/other installation; transport delivery remains concurrent by channel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connection-local windows/counters/fragments are disposed on transport loss; logical state subscriptions and generation identities remain for negotiation. Surviving resident host state avoids cold restoration. Snapshot promises are shared with reconnect installation rather than issuing another subscribe for kept snapshot-recovery channels.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reconnect diff explicitly selects snapshot recovery for kept windows and client awaits those snapshot promises. Existing restoration multiplicity and added reassembly path were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Amount of history transferred depends on active channels and replay eligibility; reconnect frequency and elapsed transfer time are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported reassembly root cause affects reconnect. Full-snapshot recovery instead of replay is an intentional state/ordering tradeoff, not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream terminal output and chat deltas while a subscribed client is slow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Server action routing now queues through the state window. Receiver action callbacks run synchronously before credit release; producer-side fire-and-forget sends are not awaited. Window exhaustion/backlogged transport delays later delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit queued direct/fragmented action notifications and cumulative channel credits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After adjacent coalescing, one delivery per queued message or fragment; credits batch by released bytes/deadline rather than one per action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each projected state action was sent directly, without state-window queuing/coalescing/credits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Flow control applies per channel and fair scheduling avoids one blocked channel monopolizing delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize incoming sends and reserialize an adjacent merged tail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reserialization touches at most a below-256-KiB tail before a merge, not an arbitrarily growing 16 MiB or history-sized string. Metadata equality is limited to adjacent matching chat deltas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Transport serialized each action independently; it did not coalesce the queued tail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server serialization occurs in the action callback; transport sending is deferred by the scheduler.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual action frequency and content bytes for distinct channels. Adjacent unsent server-originated terminal data or matching chat deltas coalesce, but only while tail text is below the effective 256 KiB frame cap; origins/rejections and different chat parts remain separate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared fair transport scheduler; independent per-channel credit windows. Data burst yields at 256 KiB and outgoing controls share a separately paced, coalescing control lane. Host action callbacks do not await sends.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This is queue coalescing, not a persistent cache. Started/partial messages are not merged. Queued text and promises are discarded on window failure/disposal; no channel history cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the bounded merge, queue and control mechanisms; no independent high-confidence regression established beyond the large-snapshot finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Output chunk sizes, slow-peer intervals and merge efficiency vary. The 256 KiB actual tail bound rejects the initially considered unbounded reserialization candidate.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: necessary accounting adds bounded work, but the proposed 16 MiB/unbounded merge cost is not the actual mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse a remote agent-host network through TCP tunnels, including upload/download, half-close and cancellation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: openTcpConnection waits for one destination connection, subscribe acceptance and the empty channel snapshot. Writes are serialized per stream and resolve after transport send; reads release credit on consumption. end/drain waits for peer credit, with consumed EOF explicitly flushing credits immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: net.createConnection to one destination, socket iterator reads, socket.write and socket.end.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination connection per requested TCP channel, with writes grouped by unchanged bounded chunks, not per byte. Host read/write directions run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same destination connection, socket operations, caps and per-direction loops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection and subscription precede stream use; socket write callbacks serialize each direction's application progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry base64 TCP notifications over AHP and expose renderer streams to the local extension host browser proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same bounded chunk deliveries, now with credits batched at 75% of the window or five seconds instead of 25%/10 ms. EOF consumption flushes credit, including queued and pending-reader cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing TCP windowing/bridge operated with more frequent credits; its underlying boundaries and write serialization already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Default bulk senders can fill the window and obtain prompt credit. Existing public drain can wait for the batching deadline when invoked before EOF; product browser end/drain consumes/flushed EOF, avoiding that delay.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Base64 encode/decode, validate notifications and route snapshots through the shared subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per unchanged bounded TCP chunk, plus a tiny initial snapshot. Receive messages remain separately capped at roughly one window plus frame/overhead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same base64 work and bounded delivery, with direct adapter release callbacks rather than shared-subscription consumption promises.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous per-message acceptance, followed by asynchronous application consumption where queued.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Opening/live sockets capped at 256 per transport and 512 per host; aggregate pending application writes capped at 16/32 MiB; 4 MiB/64-call per-stream write queues. TCP chunk/frame limits remain 16 KiB wire frames, and ordinary default receive windows match at 256 KiB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-stream writes remain Promise-chain serialized; host socket-to-stream and stream-to-socket pumps run concurrently. TCP/state channels share the fair scheduler and paced controls. Global socket/write budgets bound aggregate resource use.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: TCP channels are transport-owned and never replayed/restored. Closing, failed creation, timeout, reset and unsubscribe remove registration, stream, socket and reservations. Graceful end preserves accepted writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected destination loops, stream chunking, consumption promises, EOF flushes, browser bridge and cleanup. No standard-client deadlock or new per-chunk drain was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Foreign peers that use different/larger receive windows or applications using drain before EOF could observe the five-second batching deadline; no concrete new standard product-path regression was established for these cases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence finding. Shared-subscription refactor preserves expensive boundary counts; EOF flushing prevents the obvious graceful-shutdown latency candidate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Bind the local Automation catalogue at startup and rebind the same connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A compatible enabled connection constructs the Automation projection, synchronously parses its saved archive, and acquires a catalogue subscription. Catalogue readiness awaits its snapshot. Binding is repeated by local provider initialization and host-start notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or tear down the catalogue subscription and transfer its snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial acquisition; repeated same-connection setConnection calls now retain it. Previously clearing the final reference could unsubscribe and reacquire, causing another whole catalogue request/snapshot, not one request per automation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every setConnection cleared/rebuilt the projection, evicting and reacquiring the subscription if it was the last holder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalogue availability waits for initial snapshot, but no longer pays another readiness cycle on a redundant bind.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read cached application-storage archive text, parse archived runs and construct projected run objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per actual projection construction, rather than on every same-connection rebinding; O(archive size) per construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Redundant construction reparsed/remapped the full archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous constructor work on the renderer; underlying storage get is a service cache read, not an established new filesystem request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One catalogue resource per provider connection, deduplicated by the subscription manager while references remain live; catalogue entries and archived runs determine payload/parsing size. Rebinding the same connection now adds no work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Binding/clearing runs synchronously; initial subscribe is asynchronous and shared by live resource references. Same-connection calls are now coalesced by identity before reconstruction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: New boundConnection identity guard preserves the current store and catalogue reference. clearConnection resets the identity and disposes projections, permitting a later legitimate binding. Enablement/capability autorun remains responsible for constructing/disposing availability-dependent stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit guard, constructor work, manager reuse/disposal and counting test establish eliminated redundant work; blame provides the old mechanism's introducing commit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup ordering and whether another component also holds the catalogue determine whether redundant reconstruction additionally generated another wire subscription. Archive reconstruction was unconditional once a compatible store existed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Concrete performance fix, recorded through report_regression_fix with introducing commit 9fdeaba694c79e44cf003e20355ad67693396a19; not reported as a problem on this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unsubscribe, lose a transport, handle delivery failure, or use ordinary root/stateless/relay subscriptions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Unsubscribe routes through the channel registry and removes ownership; transport loss fails/disposes windows and clears queues before reconnect. Delivery failure reports a bounded reason and closes the connection or resets TCP. Ordinary root, relay and stateless channels retain direct delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send reset/unsubscribe/credit controls or dispose the transport; flush/clear connection-local queues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per affected channel/connection, with cumulative pending credits coalesced by method/channel. Deliberate close is not reported as a failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: TCP already had reset/unsubscribe and scheduler disposal; state channels newly share lifecycle ownership, but ordinary direct paths remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Failure disposal is immediate, with queued data rejected; control pacing can delay wire delivery within bounded queues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install IFileService.watch/createWatcher for a stateless resource-watch channel or reuse an existing channel watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher per unique watch-channel descriptor; additional subscribers increment its shared refcount. Reconnect already invoked this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same shared watcher acquisition/refcount and ordinary notification delivery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watch descriptor installation is separate from windowed state snapshot transfer; resource-watch window offers are declined.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Log a delivery failure and submit bounded role/channel-kind/reason telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per detected non-deliberate channel/control failure; no per-frame telemetry or snapshot payload transformation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing failures were logged without the newly added bounded telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Failure-path reporting only, not normal snapshot/stream processing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live channels and queued message/backlog counts; controls are capped at 16 KiB, 1024 queued entries/64 KiB and a shared token-bucket rate. State backlog limits are per channel, not a persistent history cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup traverses live channels synchronously with closed guards; controls share transport-wide bounded pacing. TCP socket reservations/leases and registrations are removed together. No newly unbounded retained cache or detached socket handle was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Disposable maps remove channels on unsubscribe and connection teardown. Fragment text, drain/snapshot waiters and queued messages are cleared/rejected; credit timers/microtasks are cancelled or guarded. Resource watches use existing shared refcounts and pending GC. Root/stateless/relay flows do not allocate accepted state windows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for traced ownership/disposal and unchanged direct delivery. New telemetry operates on small bounded classifications, not rich metadata or full snapshots.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of concurrent channels and failures varies; logging duration is unmeasured, but no normal-path amplification was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup, cache-retention or failure-reporting performance regression qualifies. Correctness-only notification/order candidates were not reported.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 19 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium-severity, high-confidence regression for newly applying repeated string-prefix flattening to large state snapshots; recorded one concrete Automation rebinding performance fix with base blame provenance. Rejected unbounded coalescing, generic per-item fan-out, TCP EOF delay and lifecycle-retention candidates after checking effective frame caps, grouping, credit flushes and disposal. Read-only static review; no execution or measured timing.
